summary: Intro call to understand LumenForge reliability requirements and map Redwood hosting options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Focus on SLOs, multi-region failover, cache/KV priming, and compliance constraints for a pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-03-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 56m | Attendees: Maya, Jordan (Redwood); Priya, Ethan, Sofia, Diego (LumenForge)

Summary: quick intros, goal is to figure out whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated (or Private) fits our SLOs and compliance. customer has bursty traffic, strict retention and wants deterministic fallbacks.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're Maya, AE on the account, and Jordan's our solutions engineer. how are you all?
00:08 Priya (LumenForge): Hi thanks, doing well. appreciate the time. we wanted to nail down precisely how you think about fallbacks and multi-region routing. we've had a couple incidents with our current provider and want a better playbook.
00:22 Jordan (Redwood SE): Absolutely. quick agenda: understand your SLOs, what's acceptable degradation, what stakeholders are involved, then map to Hosted/Dedicated/Private paths and a pilot.
00:35 Diego (LumenForge PM): Sounds good. we also need to know, uh, how the fallback impacts cost and latency — that's the big tradeoff for execs.
00:44 Ethan (SRE): yea, and from ops side, we care about KV cache priming, cold-starts, and predictable tail latency.
00:52 Jordan: great, quick qualification Qs — what's your current traffic shape and busiest window?
01:00 Ethan: average 120 rps for text gen endpoints, peaks up to 900 rps for a few minutes, daily bursts from 09:00-11:00 PST, and a machine learning inference batch at 02:00 that warms up models.
01:14 Maya: ok and are you deploying model variants today or using a single model?
01:19 Priya: single model — we haven't set up automatic fallback yet. sometimes we failover to a smaller model but it's manual. we're trying to automate that with clear SLOs.
01:30 Jordan: got it. What are your SLO targets? p99 latency, p95, error budget thresholds?
01:35 Sofia (Security): from product, we want p95 < 250ms for low-latency flows and p99 < 800ms as a stretch; any calls that violate p99 should trigger a circuit-breaker policy. error budget of 0.5% monthly. also data residency: european users must stay in eu region and logs retained for 90 days only.
01:58 Maya: OK, that helps. on the compliance side, do you need a private control plane (VPC) or is Hosted with VPC peering enough?
02:06 Sofia: preferred is VPC or Private for any PII flows. right now we classify some outputs as pseudonymous but audit team wants keys in customer KMS.
02:15 Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer KMS and on-prem, Dedicated supports customer KMS integration for keys and VPC, Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys for certain tiers — small nuance there.
02:30 Diego: can you repeat the difference quickly, sorry?
02:33 Jordan: yeah — Hosted: fastest to onboard, shared control plane, we can do CMEK for certain enterprise plans; Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in our infra with isolation and committed capacity; Private: deploys into your VPC or on-prem for full control. fallback behavior is similar across modes but routing and failover times vary.
02:52 Ethan: what does failover time typically look like between regions? if EU primary goes down, how fast can you steer to US-east?
03:00 Jordan: depends on the path. for Hosted, DNS-level steering plus health checks, usually 30-90s for steady state but in practice you want warm replicas; Dedicated with multi-region pools can be sub-15s if you keep warm instances/cold-start mitigation; Private depends on your infra. caching and KV warm-up reduces impact significantly.
03:20 Priya: warm replicas cost money — how do you optimize costs while keeping latency?
03:25 Jordan: two levers: model varianting (smaller quantized model for fallback) and prefix/KV caching to avoid recomputation. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload. also policies like gradual traffic ramp-down before failover to avoid immediate spikes.
03:40 Sofia: about audit logs and traceability — we need immutable audit logs for inference calls and token-level cost attribution. can Redwood provide that?
03:48 Maya: yes, Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and audit logs. for Private we can ship logs to your SIEM, and Dedicated can integrate with your logging pipeline.
03:58 Ethan: ok interesting. another practical question — how do you ensure model KV cache is primed across regions? we've seen cold KV miss create horrible p99s.
04:06 Jordan: good point. we support prewarming strategies: scheduled priming jobs that replay representative prefixes, and auto-prefetch for hot keys. for Dedicated we can keep persistent KV caches; for Hosted we do autoscaling with cache warmers.
04:22 Diego: do you have examples or numbers from other customers?
04:26 Jordan: yes, typical improvement is 40-70% reduction in p99 after priming for large seq lengths; we'll share anonymized benchmark sheets.
04:34 Priya: share please. also, if we use a quantized fallback model, how do you handle output quality regressions? legal wants accuracy metrics.
04:42 Maya: we recommend an A/B holdback with canary rollouts and automatic regression detection — Redwood Optimize ties evals to prompt sets so you can set thresholds.
04:52 Sofia: compliance — SSO and SAML for console access? role-based access?
04:56 Maya: yes SAML/SSO, SCIM support for user sync, and RBAC at token and route level.
05:02 Ethan: timelines — we're aiming to have a pilot in 3-4 weeks, production in 3 months if the pilot looks good.
05:08 Maya: okay that's doable. we'll propose a 4-week pilot focusing on a small subset of traffic and one critical route.
05:12 Diego: good. any gotchas around PCI/PHI? we have a healthcare vertical for a subset of customers.
05:18 Sofia: yes PHI flows must be isolated and logged. we might need on-prem for those.
05:22 Jordan: Private on-prem is the path for full PHI compliance; there are some tradeoffs with latency and ops.
05:28 Priya: question about SLA — do you offer uptime SLAs or latency SLAs?
05:33 Maya: we have uptime SLAs for Dedicated and Private (uptime %), and latency SLOs are part of our recommended configs but latency SLAs are generally part of enterprise contracts with measured baselines. we can include response-time SLOs in pilot MOP.
05:48 Diego: what's the escalation path in incidents? does Redwood bubble notifications to our on-call?
05:53 Maya: yes for Dedicated/Private we have SRE-runbooks and joint-oncall setups as an add-on, and hosted customers get health alerts + support tiers.
06:02 Ethan: can we see a playbook example for a region outage?
06:05 Jordan: sure — high level: detect via healthchecks, mark region degraded, route traffic to secondary region with model variant step-down, trigger KV prewarm in target, keep canary percent at 5% then ramp, monitor quality and fallback more aggressively if quality drops. we'll send a sample playbook.
06:24 Priya: that looks reasonable. who typically owns the canary ramp — us or Redwood?
06:29 Maya: depends on contract; pilot we'll co-own. in production, we can provide automated rollout tools but you control traffic policies.
06:36 Diego: any known limitations for multi-region in EU and APAC? we've had trouble with certain cloud providers for GPU distribution.
06:42 Jordan: availability of specific GPU SKUs in some regions can limit exact parity. in those cases we recommend model parity — using the same quantized model across regions or fallback to smaller variant in region that lacks the large GPU. acts as deterministic degradation.
06:58 Sofia: KMS integration — we need customer-managed keys that never leave our control. is that supported?
07:03 Jordan: yes for Dedicated and Private we support customer KMS/HSM. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with bring-your-own-key in enterprise plans, but key custody differs. we'll share a technical note.
07:18 Priya: what about runbook testing? can you do chaos drills with us?
07:22 Jordan: yes we support scheduled chaos drills; we can simulate zone failures and run the fallback, measure recovery time and quality. many customers use that to validate SLOs.
07:33 Ethan: if we simulate failover, is there a risk of double-billing or token accounting issues?
07:38 Maya: token accounting ties to route and model; during reroute you might see increased token usage but our billing exports will show per-token per-route attribution. we can set budget alerts.
07:50 Diego: ok great. any competitive differentiators on this front?
07:54 Maya: Redwood differentiates by unified runtime across modes and built-in routing/fallback primitives plus explicit cost controls — so you don't build the whole orchestration yourself.
08:05 Priya: fine. let's talk pilot scope briefly. we want to run a 2-week pilot under realistic traffic and then a 2-week extended soak with chaos simulation. priority route will be the low-latency path.
08:18 Jordan: recommended pilot: 2 weeks baseline data capture on Hosted evaluation or Dedicated dev pool, then 48hr stress run with bursts, then chaos drill day. we'll provide the benchmark harness.
08:30 Ethan: what metrics will you collect?
08:32 Jordan: latency p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost per response, cache hit rates, error rates, failover recovery time, and quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or custom evals).
08:44 Sofia: legal will need a copy of the SLA and data processing addendum.
08:48 Maya: we'll attach template SLA, DPA, and security pack.
08:51 Diego: how fast can you get us a price for pilot and 3-months committed Dedicated?
08:55 Maya: we'll send pilot pricing by end of week and a committed quote within 5 business days.
08:59 Priya: good. any other stakeholders we should include? we'll pull in procurement and infra on the next sync.
09:05 Maya: perfect. quick recap then next steps.
09:08 Maya (recap): 1) Redwood to share sample SLA, DPA, and KMS integration note. 2) Jordan to provision benchmark config and run initial 48hr test with your traffic sample (Ethan to share). 3) Pilot proposal and pricing (Maya). 4) Schedule pilot kickoff week of 3/27. 5) Sofia to send audit checklist.
09:29 Diego: thanks everyone.
09:31 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.
09:33 End call.

Notes / Links shared during call: - anonymized benchmark spreadsheet (link: drive.redwood/example-benchmarks) - sample fallback playbook (link: docs.redwood/fallback-playbook) - pilot proposal template (link: drive.redwood/pilot-template)
